import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# McKay conjecture

Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite group and $P \leq G$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup. Write
$$\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G) := \{\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G) : p \nmid \chi(1)\}$$
for the set of irreducible complex characters of $G$ whose degree is not divisible by $p$.
The McKay conjecture asserts that
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|,$$
where $N_G(P)$ is the normalizer of $P$ in $G$.

The conjecture was stated by McKay (1971) for $p = 2$ and simple groups, and generalized to all
primes and all finite groups by Alperin. A proof for all primes and all finite groups was
announced by Cabanes and Späth in 2023, with a manuscript available in 2024.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, McKay conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKay_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* M. Cabanes, B. Späth, *The McKay Conjecture on character degrees*,
  [arXiv:2410.20392](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20392)
-/

open CategoryTheory

namespace McKayConjecture

/--
The set $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ of irreducible complex characters of the group `G` whose degree
is not divisible by `p`.

An irreducible complex character of `G` is the character $\chi = \operatorname{tr} \circ \rho$
of an irreducible (i.e. simple) finite-dimensional complex representation `V` of `G`, and its
degree is $\chi(1) = \dim_{\mathbb C} V$. Isomorphic representations have the same character,
and over $\mathbb C$ non-isomorphic irreducible representations have distinct characters, so the
cardinality of this set is the number of irreducible complex characters of `G` of $p'$-degree,
with isomorphic representations counted once.
-/
def irrCharsDegreeNotDvd (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ ¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V ∧ V.character = χ}

/-- The degree $\chi(1)$ of a character in $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ is a natural number not
divisible by $p$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem exists_degree_of_mem_irrCharsDegreeNotDvd {p : ℕ} {G : Type} [Group G] {χ : G → ℂ}
    (h : χ ∈ irrCharsDegreeNotDvd p G) : ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ p ∣ n ∧ χ 1 = n := by
  obtain ⟨V, -, hV, rfl⟩ := h
  exact ⟨_, hV, FDRep.char_one V⟩

/--
**McKay conjecture.** Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime number and $P$ a Sylow
$p$-subgroup of $G$. Then the number of irreducible complex characters of $G$ of degree not
divisible by $p$ equals the number of irreducible complex characters of the normalizer
$N_G(P)$ of degree not divisible by $p$:
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|.$$

Since all Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ are conjugate, the right-hand side does not depend on the
choice of $P$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem mckay_conjecture (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (P : Sylow p G) :
    (irrCharsDegreeNotDvd p G).ncard =
      (irrCharsDegreeNotDvd p (P : Subgroup G).normalizer).ncard := by
  sorry

end McKayConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None on the mathematical content. The only tension is the 'open' status label versus the notes' own observation that the statement is now a theorem (Cabanes–Späth 2024); I followed the required tag and recorded the history in the docstring.
modeling_decisions: Both sides count only p'-degree characters, |Irr_{p'}(G)| = |Irr_{p'}(N_G(P))|, following the article's Statement section and Cabanes–Späth; the list entry's terse wording omits the degree restriction on the normalizer side (as the decomposition notes direct).
'Group' is read as finite group: [Finite G]. Sylow p-subgroups always exist for finite G, so the hypothesis is not vacuous.

Irreducibility is modeled by CategoryTheory.Simple in FDRep ℂ G (an abelian category, so Simple = nonzero with no proper nonzero subrepresentations), which is how Mathlib itself treats irreducible representations. The degree of χ is modeled as Module.finrank ℂ V, which equals V.character 1 (FDRep.char_one); divisibility is stated in ℕ, not in ℂ (where it would be trivial).

Counting uses Set.ncard on a set of character functions G → ℂ; for finite G this set is finite (bounded by the number of conjugacy classes), so ncard is the true cardinality and isomorphic representations are counted once, as the article requires.
G : Type rather than Type* because FDRep ℂ G requires G to live in the same universe as ℂ; every finite group is isomorphic to one in Type, so no generality is lost.
The prime hypothesis is given as the instance [Fact p.Prime], matching Mathlib's Sylow API conventions; p is otherwise an arbitrary natural number.
The right-hand side is stated for an arbitrary P : Sylow p G (universally quantified), matching 'any Sylow p-subgroup'; the docstring notes independence of the choice of P by conjugacy.

Tagged @[category research open] per the required status label, although the module docstring records that a proof was announced by Cabanes–Späth (2023, manuscript 2024); a reviewer may wish to switch to research solved with a formal_proof attribute pointing at arXiv:2410.20392.

/-!
# McKay conjecture

Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a prime. Write $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ for the set of
irreducible complex characters $\chi$ of $G$ whose degree $\chi(1)$ is not divisible by $p$.
The McKay conjecture states that $|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|$ for
any Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$, where $N_G(P)$ is the normalizer of $P$ in $G$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, McKay conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKay_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [M. Cabanes, B. Späth, *The McKay Conjecture on character degrees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20392)
-/

namespace McKayConjecture

open CategoryTheory

/-- The set $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ of irreducible complex characters of the group `G` whose
degree is not divisible by `p`.

A complex character of `G` is the function `G → ℂ` sending `g` to the trace of `g` acting on a
finite-dimensional complex representation `V` of `G`. It is irreducible when `V` is irreducible,
i.e. a simple object of `FDRep ℂ G`. Its degree `χ(1)` is the dimension of `V`
(see `FDRep.char_one`).

Irreducible complex characters of a finite group determine the representation up to
isomorphism, so the cardinality of this set is the number of irreducible complex representations
of `G` of dimension not divisible by `p`, with isomorphic representations counted once. -/
def irrCharsPrimeTo (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ ∧ ¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V}

/-- The degree `χ(1)` of a character in $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ is a natural number not
divisible by `p`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem exists_eq_apply_one_of_mem_irrCharsPrimeTo {p : ℕ} {G : Type} [Group G] {χ : G → ℂ}
    (hχ : χ ∈ irrCharsPrimeTo p G) : ∃ n : ℕ, χ 1 = n ∧ ¬ p ∣ n := by
  obtain ⟨V, -, rfl, hV⟩ := hχ
  exact ⟨_, V.char_one, hV⟩

/-- **McKay conjecture.** Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $P$ be a Sylow
$p$-subgroup of $G$. Then the number of irreducible complex characters of $G$ of degree not
divisible by $p$ equals the number of irreducible complex characters of the normalizer
$N_G(P)$ of degree not divisible by $p$, that is,
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|.$$
Here isomorphic representations are counted once. The statement does not depend on the choice
of $P$, since all Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ are conjugate.

The list entry on Wikipedia omits the restriction "of degree not divisible by $p$" on the
normalizer side; the statement given in the Wikipedia article on the McKay conjecture includes
it on both sides, as formalised here.

A proof of the conjecture was announced by Cabanes and Späth in 2023 (manuscript 2024). -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem mckay_conjecture (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (P : Sylow p G) :
    (irrCharsPrimeTo p G).ncard = (irrCharsPrimeTo p (P : Subgroup G).normalizer).ncard := by
  sorry

end McKayConjecture

G is taken in Type (universe 0) because FDRep ℂ G requires k and G in the same universe as ℂ; every finite group is isomorphic to one in Type, so no generality is lost.

Category tag is `research open` as mandated by the task's status label, even though the conjecture is now regarded as proved (Cabanes–Späth, arXiv:2410.20392); the docstring mentions the announced proof. Reviewers may prefer `research solved` with a `formal_proof using informal` attribute.
The normalizer N_G(P) is formalised as the subgroup (P : Subgroup G).normalizer coerced to a type with its inherited Group structure.

    Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ (n : ℕ) (ρ : Representation ℂ G (Fin n → ℂ)),
    IsSimpleModule (MonoidAlgebra ℂ G) ρ.asModule ∧
      (fun g ↦ LinearMap.trace ℂ (Fin n → ℂ) (ρ g)) = χ ∧ ¬p ∣ n}

$$\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G) := \{\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G) : p \nmid \chi(1)\}$$

$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|,$$
where $N_G(P)$ is the normalizer of $P$ in $G$.

all finite groups by Alperin. A proof for all primes and all finite groups was announced by
Cabanes and Späth in 2023, with a manuscript available in 2024.

* [Wikipedia, McKay conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKay_conjecture)

* M. Cabanes, B. Späth, *The McKay Conjecture on character degrees*,
  [arXiv:2410.20392](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20392)

namespace McKayConjecture

/--

is not divisible by `p`.

of irreducible complex characters of `G` of degree not divisible by `p`.
-/
def irrP' (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ ¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V ∧ V.character = χ}

Späth in 2023.

- [Wikipedia, *McKay conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKay_conjecture)

- [M. Cabanes, B. Späth, *The McKay Conjecture on character degrees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20392)
-/

degree is not divisible by $p$. A character is the function `G → ℂ` sending `g` to the trace of

character is the dimension of the underlying representation, i.e. $\chi(1)$. Since isomorphic
representations have the same character, each isomorphism class of irreducible representations
is counted once. -/
def irrCharsPrimeToDeg (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ ∧ ¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V}

/-- Every $\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ satisfies $\chi(1) = n$ for a natural number $n$ with
$p \nmid n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem exists_eq_apply_one_of_mem_irrCharsPrimeToDeg {p : ℕ} {G : Type} [Group G]
    {χ : G → ℂ} (hχ : χ ∈ irrCharsPrimeToDeg p G) : ∃ n : ℕ, χ 1 = n ∧ ¬ p ∣ n := by
  obtain ⟨V, -, rfl, hV⟩ := hχ
  exact ⟨Module.finrank ℂ V, FDRep.char_one V, hV⟩

of $G$. Then the number of irreducible complex characters of $G$ of degree not divisible by $p$
equals the number of irreducible complex characters of the normalizer $N_G(P)$ of degree not
divisible by $p$:

the right-hand side does not depend on the choice of $P$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem mckay_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G) :
    (irrCharsPrimeToDeg p G).ncard = (irrCharsPrimeToDeg p P.normalizer).ncard := by

end McKayConjecture
